Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently delivered a talk at the Startup School 2026 event, and the video of her speech has been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel. You can watch it below.

Susan Kare shared wonderful stories and design insights

More than 40 years have passed since the launch of the original Macintosh, but the system's graphics, fonts, icons and overall UI elements still look as captivating today as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh remain part of macOS to this day, preserved both in spirit and in appearance. From the Command key symbol and the "Happy Mac" startup icon, to the system fonts and the hand-shaped cursor, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac, but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone who has studied Apple's history may have seen Kare's sketches and even read or heard her discuss these early works in interviews, hearing her speak first-hand about the passion and frustration of working on graphical user interfaces and pixel art when it was still uncharted territory remains fascinating.

So, if you have an interest in design, are curious about Apple's history, or simply enjoy hearing someone share their lifelong passion from a professional perspective, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple, Kare also discussed how she joined the company, showed works created after she left, shared some anecdotes from Apple's early days, and quoted other legendary designers to bring further inspiration to the audience.
